correctness.rationale: For k>=2, h=2^k-1, a binary [h,h-k,3] Hamming perfect code has a weight-three word, so its two parity classes have equal size 2^(h-k-1). Same-parity distinct codewords have distance >=4, hence their closed radius-one balls form induced h-stars. Alternating parity with the passive-fiber parity prevents cross-fiber endpoint adjacencies; the selected edge count is h*2^(d-k-1) for all d>=h, giving Q9>=224. For Q5 an independent exact maximum-clique search in the 80-edge compatibility graph, anchored at one edge by edge-transitivity, found maximum 12 and 12 anchored maximizers, hence 80 total; every optimizer is one of the 80 separately constructed 4x3-edge-star packings. Correctness does not assert Q9 optimality.
